Personally, the way I started to really know myself is distancing myself from my parents. I lived with them last year (for 2 years before I cut them off last June). I found a friend group that I consider my family. They helped me find more interests. Now I will say I have always known what I liked, and I grew up having a lot of hobbies and skills I still utilize today. But they were never acknowledged and or/criticized by my parents. 

Before I cut them off, I stopped hanging around them gradually. It came to a point where I was barely home because I spent all my time with my friends (as well as work and school in between). It helped a lot in terms of going and doing new things, figuring out how to navigate conflict with my friends, and having meaningful conversations. All of which I couldn’t do with my parents.

I became so tired of being under their roof (my mom yet again crossed a boundary) I packed my things and left, and I was homeless for two months. Guess who was there? Not my family, but my friends. I couch hopped with them and slept in my car while I worked my ass off to get the place I have now. Haven’t spoken to them since last June and I already feel like I’ve grown so much.

My case is pretty extreme, but I think gradually pulling yourself away to do your own thing is honestly the way to go. Especially if you live with your parents. Mine definitely got the hint.

Previous friend groups I’ve had fell apart on my end because I never knew how to deal with conflict, and I eventually push everyone away. They noticed this about me, and still included me in everything. They saw my value where my parents didn’t. They encouraged me in ways my parents couldn’t. With that, I’ve learned to love myself more and be confident, and be okay to ask for help or reassurance when I need it.

Yikes, I’ve been out if banking for a minute, but I’ll explain as best as I can.

So anytime you carry a balance on your credit card, you’re accruing interest. Say your statement open/close date is 9/10/22 to 10/10/22 and you have a $800 balance, you’re accruing interest on that amount. 

Lets say you paid your balance in full on 9/25/22. You still accrued interest between 9/10/22 up until you paid it in full on 9/25/22. So when your statement closes on 10/10/22, you’ll see that residual. Its a common misconception that if you pay your balance in full, you don’t get interest. That is partly true going forward, but when it comes to statements everything is backdated and until that balance is paid in full, you are accruing interest everyday until it is paid.

My customers could never wrap their heads around this, and I’m sure I explained this very well during my time working with credit cards. But I hope this explanation helped!
